title: What is a safe temperature for a fridge?
desc: The safe temperature for a refrigerator is 40°F (4°C) or below. Keeping foods at the proper temperatures is one of the best ways to slow the growth of bacteria. The freezer should be set at 0°F (-18°C).

title: What are the rules for a new refrigerator?
desc: Once the refrigerator is in your home, follow these steps: Leave the fridge to sit for 3 hours. Then plug it in and turn it on. Allow it to stabilise overnight before placing any fresh food inside.

title: How long does a refrigerator last?
desc: Most refrigerators are designed to last between 10 and 20 years. If your fridge is over ten years old and experiencing issues, replacing it rather than investing in repairs may save you more money in the long run.

title: How to control fridge temperature?
desc: To control the temperature of your fridge, locate the temperature controls on the interior or exterior control panel. These may be dials, sliders, or digital displays. Adjust the settings according to the manufacturer's instructions to achieve the desired temperature range (typically 35°F to 38°F for the fridge and -18°F or below for the freezer).

title: How long does it take for a fridge to cool?
desc: A running refrigerator typically starts to cool within a few hours after being turned on for the first time, but it may take up to 24 hours to reach its optimal temperature range. Owners should wait at least 24 hours for a new refrigerator to fully cool down before loading it with perishable items.

title: How to know if a fridge is working?
desc:
Here are seven significant warning signs that your refrigerator may be malfunctioning:
1. It’s not cold enough.
2. Your food is spoiling quickly.
3. There's condensation inside.
4. Ice is building up in the freezer.
5. The motor is hot.
6. It’s making loud noises.
7. There's water on the floor.

title: Why is my fridge not cooling?
desc: Several factors can cause a refrigerator not to cool properly, including dirty condenser coils, poor ventilation, improper installation, faulty or dirty gasket seals, disorganized food storage, placement of the appliance, and malfunctioning internal parts.

title: Does a fridge cool faster when empty or full?
desc: The optimal way to fill a fridge is to have it about three-quarters full. This allows for sufficient air circulation while still having enough food to help cool neighboring items.

title: How to check the fridge thermostat?
desc: To check a fridge thermostat, you will need a multimeter and some basic knowledge of how it works. First, disconnect the fridge from the power source. Set the multimeter to the ohms setting and test the thermostat’s terminals for resistance. At room temperature, you should get a reading between 0 and 1 ohm. If the reading is inconsistent with the thermostat's setting, it may be faulty and need replacement.

title: Why is my refrigerator cooling less?
desc: Over time, dust and debris can accumulate on the condenser coils, reducing your refrigerator's cooling efficiency. To fix this, clean the coils using a vacuum cleaner with a brush attachment or a coil cleaning brush to remove built-up dirt.
